mandate_description: In its resolution 2796 (2025), the Security Council encouraged UNSMIL to implement the recommendations of the 2025 Strategic Review (S/2025/611), including to: (a) place the support of a political solution to the Libyan conflict at the core of the Mission’s mandate and streamline its workstreams to that end; (b) establish a more consistent presence across Libya, including targeted expansions in Benghazi and Sabha, while maintaining a cost neutral realignment and within existing resources; (c) increase engagement in eastern and southern Libya with key stakeholders to support reunification efforts; (d) establish a dedicated economic unit within UNSMIL; (e) assume a leading role in international engagement on Libya, particularly in relation to the Berlin Process, encouraging its full participation and continued evolution and inclusivity to further advance the process; and recognize that UNSMIL’s engagement on human rights and the rule of law remains integral to the country’s political process.

mandate_description: In its resolution 2814 (2026), the Security Council revised the mandate of BINUH to focus on: (a) Support the Haitian authorities on their efforts to organize and hold municipal, parliamentary and presidential elections and achieve a peaceful transfer of power to elected Haitian officials; (b) Coordinate international electoral assistance to Haiti in cooperation with other regional and international stakeholders; (c) Support Haitian authorities in efforts to reduce community violence, and assist in the design of a Haitian-led disarmament, dismantlement, and reintegration program; (d) Support Haitian authorities in addressing prolonged pretrial detention, provide  support to the Haitian judiciary in the monitoring of the functioning of the courts  and for its handling of high-risk individuals; and (d) monitor and report on cases of gang violence, criminal activities, and human rights abuses and violations, including sexual violence, as well as assist national authorities in strengthening respect for human rights.
